owner_signal.interpretation: v8 is non-discriminating because its descendants preserve the same bar-conduction timing law. Do not ask the owner to rank tiny mix or handoff deltas until the timing law itself changes.
owner_signal.statement: All v8 cuts share the same dominant audible defect: the instrumental feels as if it begins at one tempo and is then dragged down to match the vocal.

review_policy.reason_control_omitted: The owner already identified the inherited bar-conduction signature as the dominant defect; replaying it adds burden without information.

terminal_logic.next_after_review: lock the preferred timing law, then reapply only previously positive arc and production modules under that law

timing_laws.label: single-speed
timing_laws.mechanism: replace all per-bar donor-band tempo scales with one constant passage-wide tempo scale chosen to preserve the original conducted core span; reflow donor-band clips continuously from the first cue
timing_laws.tempo_rule: one constant scale across the entire donor band
timing_laws.why: tests the old-school single pitch-fader hypothesis: one tempo match, then let the band play

timing_laws.label: native-pocket
timing_laws.mechanism: set donor-band tempo scale to 1.0 and reflow the band continuously from the first cue, preserving the native donor pocket and accepting natural drift
timing_laws.why: tests whether preserving the drummer's native feel beats synchronization

timing_laws.label: phrase-reset
timing_laws.mechanism: use one constant donor-band tempo scale per four-slot phrase, chosen to fit that phrase's original conducted span, and reset phase only at phrase boundaries
timing_laws.phase_rule: re-cue only at four-slot phrase boundaries
timing_laws.tempo_rule: one constant tempo scale per four-slot phrase
timing_laws.why: tests DJ-style nudging: preserve a stable pocket inside each phrase and hide synchronization changes at phrase boundaries instead of dragging every bar
